name: Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance
guide:
Governance, risk, and compliance work is about proving that security controls exist and actually function, not about designing them from scratch. A typical week includes running risk assessments against a defined framework, preparing evidence for an external audit, tracking remediation items after a penetration test, and briefing internal stakeholders on where controls are weak. This is different from Security Leadership, which owns the architecture, the incident response program, and the engineering roadmap that GRC then measures. It is also different from Privacy and Data Protection, which focuses specifically on personal data handling, consent, and regulations like GDPR, while GRC covers the broader control environment across security, operational, and sometimes financial risk.

Readers often confuse the three because postings overlap in language. A Security GRC role at an AI lab, for example, might reference NIST or FedRAMP the same way a Security Leadership role does, but the GRC person is auditing whether the control is met, not building the system that meets it. A privacy-focused role will center on GDPR and consumer data flows specifically, while a GRC-titled role in our sample tends to reference GDPR alongside SOC 2, ISO 27001, and NIST as one framework among several. If a posting talks mainly about designing systems or leading a security org, it likely belongs in Security Leadership. If it talks mainly about consent, data subject requests, or privacy impact assessments, it likely belongs in Privacy and Data Protection.

Our sample does not carry a dedicated certifications field, so we cannot say with confidence which specific credentials, such as CISA or CRISC, appear in these 121 postings tracked under this category. What the data does show clearly is which frameworks recur, and ISO 27001 appears in 31 of the 121 postings, often tied to lead auditor style responsibilities rather than listed as a decorative line. SOC 2 appears in 28 postings and NIST in 31, both treated as frameworks a GRC hire is expected to already know rather than learn on the job. A degree in a related field like information security or business shows up across these postings, but the language suggests framework knowledge and audit experience carry more weight than the credential itself.

Experience requirements skew senior in our sample, with 62 of 121 postings labeled Senior, compared to 31 Mid-level, 15 Manager, and only 2 Junior and 1 Intern posting. That skew is partly a data artifact, since one company, Marathon Petroleum, accounts for 44 of the 121 postings, all variants of the same senior GRC automation role posted across many Texas locations. Outside that cluster, hiring still favors people with three or more years doing audits or risk assessments over entry level candidates. Junior roles do exist in the sample, but they are a small minority, and the more common path in looks like an analyst-level audit or compliance background before moving into a titled GRC role.

The tools and frameworks named most often in our data are AWS, appearing in 35 postings, followed by ISO 27001 and NIST at 31 each, SOC 2 at 28, GDPR at 17, GCP at 16, and Azure at 15. FedRAMP shows up in 12 postings, concentrated among government-adjacent employers, and HIPAA appears in 12 as well, mostly at health-adjacent or platform companies. AI Governance appears in 11 postings, reflecting how many AI labs in our sample, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are building dedicated GRC functions around model risk. Vulnerability management and general cloud security tooling appear in a smaller but consistent share of postings.

We currently track approximately 32 open postings in this category as of the most recent data pull. Of the 121 postings in our broader sample, 67 carried an explicit salary figure, and among those the range ran from $82,842 to $376,326 per year, with most values clustered between $150,000 and $220,000. That range is heavily influenced by the Marathon Petroleum postings and by Adzuna-sourced listings that report a single point figure rather than a true minimum and maximum, so treat it as directional rather than precise. Beyond Marathon Petroleum, the companies appearing most often hiring for this category include Guidehouse, OpenAI, Cloudflare, Palantir, Nebius, xAI, Anthropic, and Sierra, spanning consulting firms, cloud platforms, and AI labs.
